title: Warehouse queue on a skewed Status: a filtered index is requested
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
Ticket from the warehouse product owner: 'Create a filtered index for active statuses. The queue screen only shows
active orders.' The missing-index DMV suggests equality WarehouseId, Status; include CustomerId, PromisedShipDate,
Priority; impact 88%. Decide which index to create.

sql: SELECT TOP (500) o.OrderId, o.CustomerId, o.PromisedShipDate, o.Priority
FROM dbo.Orders o WHERE o.WarehouseId = @WarehouseId AND o.Status = @Status
workload.plan: Index Seek IX_Orders_Status (Status = @Status) with residual WarehouseId, Key Lookup PK_Orders (about 9,200 rows, for Priority), Sort, Top.

workload.sql: UPDATE dbo.Orders SET Status = @Status, UpdatedAt = SYSUTCDATETIME() WHERE OrderId = @OrderId;
workload.plan: Maintains IX_Orders_CustomerId_OrderDate, IX_Orders_CustomerId_Wide, IX_Orders_Status and IX_Orders_ChannelId_UpdatedAt.

facts: dbo.Orders: 182M rows, 350k inserts a day, about 2.1M status updates a day, 340k invoice updates a day.
Status: 1 Pending 0.01%, 2 Released 0.06% (about 110k rows), 3 Picking 0.02%, 4 Packed 0.01%, 7 Shipped 0.4%, 8 Cancelled 2.9%, 9 Completed 96.6%.

Q4 is parameterized on @Status. A filtered index is not matched by a predicate on a parameter; the procedure needs a literal predicate such as Status IN (1,2,3,4) for the queue path. The procedure can be changed within 2 working days.
A legacy job updates dbo.Orders from sqlcmd without the -I switch, so its session has QUOTED_IDENTIFIER OFF. An update of a table with a filtered index fails with error 1934 in such a session.
Q4 sorts by PromisedShipDate, Priority DESC and returns 500 rows.

create.why: The key continues with the ORDER BY columns, so TOP 500 reads 500 rows in order with no sort and no lookup. The filtered form holds about 0.1% of the table; the unfiltered form needs no procedure change.

must_not_create.why: It ignores ORDER BY PromisedShipDate, Priority DESC and leaves a sort of every matching row.
IX_Orders_Status already does this, and it is the plan that needs 9,200 lookups and a sort.

key.reference_notes: Not scored here: the procedure change that lets the filtered index match, the sqlcmd -I fix that must come first, and keeping IX_Orders_Status until the new index is proven.
